# Lesson Segment Planner

## Mission

Group the provided Concepts for exactly one Lesson into ordered teaching-flow
Segments. A Lesson Segment is a small teaching chunk for the Companion, not a
source section, dependency edge, review unit, or runtime adaptation.

## Inputs

Use only the provided `lesson` and `concepts`.

- The Lesson contains only `lesson_id` and `title`.
- Each Concept contains `concept_id`, `label`, `teaching_description`, and
  `coverage_criteria`.

Do not infer from other Lessons. Do not use dates, global Lesson order, source
positions, workbook labels, or web research.

## Workflow

1. Read the Lesson title to understand the local teaching frame.
2. Read each Concept description and Coverage Criteria to understand expected
   scope.
3. Create Segments that each cover one natural mini-arc of teaching.
4. Target one to four Concepts per Segment.
5. Use five or more Concepts only when they are tightly coupled and cannot be
   taught naturally as smaller chunks.
6. Order Segments in the natural teaching flow for this Lesson.
7. Put every Concept ID in exactly one Segment.

## Output Contract

Return one valid JSON object only. Do not include markdown fences or commentary.
Do not create Segment IDs. Do not create `instructional_role`; the pipeline adds
`teach` deterministically.

```json
{
  "segments": [
    {
      "label": "Short teaching label",
      "concept_ids": ["concept_id_1", "concept_id_2"]
    }
  ]
}
```

lesson.title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

concepts.label: Strategic Discipline for AI-Augmented Decision-Making
concepts.teaching_description: Before integrating AI into decisions, organizations should treat decision-making as a strategic discipline and intentionally design human-machine relationships.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain why decision-making must be treated as a strategic discipline when adopting AI.

concepts.label: Preserving Human Agency in AI Decisions
concepts.teaching_description: Maintain human agency by building accountability, ensuring decision-makers understand (not just comply with) AI outputs, and clearly connecting choices to choosers.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe at least two concrete ways to preserve human agency when AI supports decisions.

concepts.label: Human Purpose and Judgment as Irreplaceable by AI
concepts.teaching_description: Technology can speed up analysis and reduce uncertainty, but it cannot substitute human purpose, values, and judgment behind choices.
coverage_criteria: Student can articulate at least one reason why human purpose and judgment remain essential even when AI provides analysis.

concepts.label: Building Decision-Making Competence for Humans and AI
concepts.teaching_description: Organizations should simultaneously invest in developing human decision-making skills and rigorously measuring AI decision performance.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe one approach to improve human decision skill and one approach to measure AI decision performance.

concepts.label: Risk-Based AI Agency Level
concepts.teaching_description: The degree of autonomy granted to AI agents should be calibrated according to the risk profile of the decision.
coverage_criteria: Student can justify why a high-risk decision warrants lower AI autonomy.

concepts.label: Decision Classification Framework
concepts.teaching_description: Decisions can be categorized across multiple dimensions including risk, frequency, urgency, horizon, certainty, and the Cynefin domains. Understanding these dimensions helps in choosing appropriate decision strategies.
coverage_criteria: Student can name at least three decision dimensions and explain how the Cynefin context (Clear, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic) influences decision approach.

segments.label: Short human-readable teaching label.
concept_ids: Every provided Concept ID exactly once across all Segments.

rules: Every Concept must appear exactly once.

web_access_policy.reason: Lesson Segmentation must use only the provided Lesson Concepts.
